methodology: Treat transport bytes, semantic projection, unknown-field behavior, and transformation loss as separate questions.
Prefer publisher specifications and documentation. Mark behavior not stated by those sources as not-specified rather than inferring compatibility.
Use descriptions of harmless structural samples; this study does not redistribute provider payloads.

ecosystems.name: OpenAI Responses API

transport.mode: HTTPS request/response; streaming uses server-sent events
transport.framing: Named semantic events are delivered as SSE data
transport.capture_surface: Client, reverse proxy, or SDK transport hook before parsing

projection.model: Response objects and typed lifecycle/content delta events
projection.granularity: Response, output item, content part, and delta
projection.semantic_mapping: SDKs project SSE JSON into typed response events

unknown_fields.scope: The API reference does not promise that SDK parsing and reserialization retain future JSON members

known_losses: Typed projections need not retain SSE delimiters, header order, JSON whitespace, or unmodeled members

samples.shape: response.output_text.delta event containing a delta and identifiers
samples.research_use: Exercise the boundary between captured SSE bytes and the typed event projection

conclusions: A typed event stream is not proof of exact request or response byte retention.
open_questions: Which official SDK versions preserve unrecognized event types and members?
limitations: Documentation describes protocol semantics, not every intermediary or SDK implementation.

sources.title: Streaming API responses
sources.claim_supported: The Responses API exposes typed streaming events including response and output-text lifecycle events.

ecosystems.name: Anthropic Messages API

transport.mode: HTTPS; streaming uses server-sent events
transport.framing: SSE events carry message, content-block, ping, and error event payloads
transport.capture_surface: Client or gateway before the SDK combines content deltas

projection.model: Message/content-block lifecycle with typed deltas
projection.semantic_mapping: Events may be accumulated into a final Message object

unknown_fields.scope: Anthropic states clients should handle unknown event types gracefully; this is forward-compatible handling, not an exact-byte guarantee

known_losses: Accumulating deltas loses original SSE framing and may lose unknown-event payloads depending on the client

samples.shape: message_start, content_block_delta, and message_stop SSE events
samples.research_use: Compare event order and partial JSON deltas with a final projected message

conclusions: Unknown event tolerance does not imply that an SDK stores or re-emits unknown events.
open_questions: Do all maintained SDK stream helpers expose raw unknown events to callers?
limitations: The source gives client guidance but does not specify intermediary retention.

sources.title: Streaming Messages
sources.claim_supported: Message streaming uses SSE, defines typed events and deltas, and instructs clients to handle unknown event types gracefully.

ecosystems.name: Google Gemini generateContent API

transport.mode: REST or RPC; streamGenerateContent supports an SSE mode
transport.framing: A stream of GenerateContentResponse values
transport.capture_surface: HTTP/RPC client or gateway before SDK object conversion

projection.model: Content, Part, Candidate, usage, citation, and safety objects
projection.granularity: Candidate and content part per streamed response
projection.semantic_mapping: SDKs project wire responses into language-specific response objects

unknown_fields.scope: The API reference does not guarantee retention of unknown JSON members by SDK objects

known_losses: SDK aggregation can lose response chunk boundaries, serialization details, and future fields

samples.shape: GenerateContentResponse with candidate content parts and usage metadata
samples.research_use: Test chunk-order capture separately from final candidate text

conclusions: Gemini semantic content objects should be linked to, not substituted for, transport capture.
open_questions: How do current SDKs expose unknown Part variants and response fields?
limitations: REST, RPC, and SDK transports may produce different observable framing.

sources.title: Gemini API: models.streamGenerateContent
sources.claim_supported: The API streams GenerateContentResponse objects and documents SSE as a supported streaming response mode.

ecosystems.name: Amazon Bedrock Runtime

transport.mode: HTTPS with AWS event-stream responses for streaming inference
transport.framing: Binary AWS event-stream frames contain model response chunks and exception events
transport.capture_surface: SigV4-aware client or gateway before event-stream decoding

projection.model: Provider-specific body inside Bedrock chunk and exception envelope types
projection.semantic_mapping: SDK decodes the envelope; model body remains dependent on the selected model

unknown_fields.scope: The Runtime reference does not promise preservation of unknown provider body fields after model-specific decoding

known_losses: A unified projection can erase AWS event headers, binary frame boundaries, and provider-specific payload members

samples.shape: PayloadPart bytes or a modeled exception event
samples.research_use: Retain envelope and payload boundaries before provider-specific parsing

conclusions: Bedrock has both an AWS envelope and a model-specific inner format; both layers matter.
open_questions: Which managed gateways expose the original AWS event-stream headers and CRC-protected frames?
limitations: Model-specific bodies vary and cannot be treated as one Bedrock semantic schema.

sources.title: InvokeModelWithResponseStream
sources.claim_supported: Streaming model invocation returns an AWS event stream with payload-part and modeled exception events.

ecosystems.name: OpenAI-compatible APIs

transport.mode: Typically OpenAI-shaped HTTP JSON and SSE endpoints
transport.framing: Implementation-specific subset of OpenAI request, response, and SSE shapes
transport.capture_surface: Compatibility endpoint before client normalization

projection.model: A claimed subset or extension of OpenAI chat/message objects
projection.granularity: Request, response, choice, message, and delta
projection.semantic_mapping: Compatibility adapters translate an implementation's native model into OpenAI-shaped fields

unknown_fields.scope: Compatibility is not a versioned universal contract; accepted and returned extensions vary

known_losses: Native finish reasons, tool semantics, usage accounting, errors, and extensions may be approximated or omitted

samples.shape: Chat-completions-style messages with streaming enabled
samples.research_use: Compare accepted fields and returned event shapes across implementations

conclusions: The label OpenAI-compatible is a test target, not evidence of wire or semantic equivalence.
open_questions: Which compatibility version and extension set does each deployment claim?
limitations: TGI is one concrete counterexample to a universal compatibility profile, not a survey of every implementation.

sources.title: Messages API
sources.claim_supported: TGI offers an OpenAI Chat Completions compatible Messages API, demonstrating that compatibility is implemented by a distinct server.

unknown_fields.scope: JSON-RPC extensibility exists, but retention by SDK models and middleware is not a protocol-wide exact-byte promise

transport.capture_surface: AutoGen event/logger handler; provider transport must be captured separately

projection.model: Agent messages, tool calls/results, model-call events, usage, and runtime events
projection.semantic_mapping: Provider responses become AutoGen message and event types

ecosystems.name: OpenTelemetry Protocol

transport.mode: Protobuf over gRPC or HTTP; JSON-encoded protobuf over HTTP is also defined
transport.framing: Export requests group resource, scope, and signal data
transport.capture_surface: OTLP receiver before protobuf/JSON decoding

projection.model: Resources, instrumentation scopes, traces, metrics, logs, and profiles
projection.granularity: Batch, resource, scope, and signal record
projection.semantic_mapping: Telemetry SDKs project application events into OTLP signal schemas

unknown_fields.scope: Binary protobuf parsers generally retain unknown fields in many runtimes, while protobuf JSON parsers reject unknown fields by default unless configured to ignore them

known_losses: JSON conversion changes encoding and field names; collectors may batch, sample, truncate, filter, or transform attributes

samples.shape: ResourceSpans containing ScopeSpans and spans
samples.research_use: Test binary and JSON unknown-field behavior separately

conclusions: OTLP transport capture and decoded telemetry are different artifacts; protobuf and JSON need separate conformance cases.
open_questions: Which collector processors preserve protobuf unknown fields end to end?
limitations: Unknown-field behavior also depends on protobuf runtime and collector transformations.

projection.semantic_mapping: Provider/framework details map into conventional attributes and event bodies

ecosystems.name: Raw Envoy and NGINX gateway logs

transport.framing: Configured text/JSON access-log records; body and streaming frames are not present by default
transport.capture_surface: Proxy filters, taps, or packet/application capture with explicit authorization

projection.model: Configured request/response metadata such as method, path, status, duration, bytes, and selected headers
projection.granularity: Usually one access record per request
projection.semantic_mapping: Format variables project proxy state into text or structured JSON

cross_ecosystem_conclusions: Transport capture, framework events, telemetry conventions, and observability backends are complementary layers. None should silently stand in for another.
Exact-byte claims require capture before parsing plus digest and provenance. Parsed JSON, SDK objects, spans, and access logs cannot establish byte identity.
Unknown-field behavior must be tested for each parser, SDK, collector, exporter, and backend version. Protocol extensibility alone is insufficient.
Compatibility labels describe intent or a subset. They do not establish equivalent errors, streaming, tools, usage, extensions, or retention.
global_limitations: This is documentation research, not packet-level conformance testing.
Hosted services and SDKs can change without preserving old documentation; adapters must pin and test versions.
The listed framework and platform projections may omit content intentionally for privacy, cost, or security.
No system can provide perfect safety. Trace completeness does not establish semantic correctness or policy authority.
